assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ab initio molecular dynamics put electronic structure and nuclear motion in one simple scheme, making condensed-phase and reactive chemistry computable from first principles. It is a clear game-changer with four decades of consequences in liquids, solids, solvation and enzyme-related modelling, and it connects quantitatively to experiment.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is the unambiguous origin; two laureates map cleanly onto it, which fits the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently adopted across chemistry, physics and materials science; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with DFT recognition (1998) and with Parrinello's roles in metadynamics and machine-learned potentials; I have not independently verified all citation history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand cleavage by using deaminase chemistry on DNA. It is conceptually simple and already has real consequences in disease models and clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab made the decisive and generalizable contribution (cytosine and adenine base editors). The independent Target-AID work of Nishida and Kondo is a credit question, so a single laureate is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade old but with broad independent replication and clinical translation; slightly early for the long-term clinical record.
uncertainties: Whether Nishida and Kondo warrant co-credit.
Prime editing (a separate entry) is closely tied to the same laureate and could be recognized jointly or later.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity degradation is a new therapeutic modality: a small molecule recruits an E3 ligase to destroy a target. It redefined what counts as druggable and degraders are now in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, underpinning molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito and others are also credible, so allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well confirmed, but clinical approvals of degraders are still pending, so this may be slightly premature.
uncertainties: Fair split between PROTAC and molecular glue contributions is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing is a technological game-changer for biology and medicine built on sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, with consequences that are enormous and proven.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa reversible-terminator approach, while Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing was a parallel pioneering route; Mayer and Ju also have claims, so priority is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with clear independent confirmation and global use.
uncertainties: Sanger sequencing was recognized earlier, and the contribution may be viewed as primarily technological or medical.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed amino acids site-specifically, giving chemists direct access to protein structure and function in living systems. It is new, clear and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the orthogonal tRNA/synthetase approach in vivo; Chin extended it to eukaryotes and multi-site and reassigned codons. Mehl and Yokoyama are less likely to be decisive.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated over two decades with many applications; timely.
uncertainties: Ordering and weighting of Schultz, Wang and Chin.
Overlap with Flexizyme/genetic reprogramming work in other entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials give near-quantum accuracy at classical cost, changing what can be simulated in chemistry and materials. It matches my own field's need for quantitatively validated simulation and has already shown real consequences.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello's 2007 neural-network potential and Csányi and Bartók's Gaussian approximation potentials are separate foundations. I propose Behler and Csányi to avoid duplicating Parrinello, but credit is an open question.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing and widely adopted, though reliability and transferability limits are still being explored, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether Parrinello should instead be included.
Fast-moving field with many contributors, including the foundation-model generation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory gave a quantitative physical framework for how proteins fold and for why folding is fast, connecting theory to experiment. It is a fundamental conceptual contribution.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are most associated with the funnel formalism, and Dill with the hydrophobic-collapse framework; Bryngelson and Fersht's experimental mapping are important and the allocation is tricky.
assessment.maturity: Mature conceptually, though its relation to the 2024 prize and to the predictive-structure revolution complicates timing.
uncertainties: Ordering among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and the experimental side (Fersht).
Possible perception of overlap with the 2024 recognition of structure prediction.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry measures intact assemblies, stoichiometry and interactions, which is a real and quantitative structural capability that complements cryo-EM and crystallography.
assessment.attribution: Robinson most clearly brought it to routine intact complexes, Chait and Heck contributed methodology and applications; Loo and Gross also have claims, so credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Mature with broad independent adoption, though ESI was already recognized in 2002.
uncertainties: Risk that it is seen as an incremental extension of an already awarded ionization technology.
